name: term_neonate_12h
description: Literature reference values for a healthy term neonate (~3.5 kg) at ~12 h after an uncomplicated vaginal birth (the same baby as term_neonate_72h, cord clamping as there), room air, dressed or skin-to-skin, breastfeeding started. Grades: A = healthy term at that age, B = nearby age or related population, C = textbook/derived/carried from 72 h.
state: calm, quiet awake or asleep, dressed/skin-to-skin at room temperature

variables.label: Heart rate
variables.method: auscultation at 2 h, healthy term, any delivery mode
variables.notes: P50 120-122 after 2 h (Tveiten); range: the 2 h P2-P98 spread shifted to the 12 h median.

variables.label: Systolic BP
variables.notes: Healthy controls: 67.4 at birth, 69.2 at 6 h, 69.8 at 12 h, 71.3 at 24 h, 71.8 at 48 h (Taiwo 2022, mean BW 3.05 kg).

variables.label: Diastolic BP
variables.notes: 37.1 at birth, 38.0 at 6 h, 40.4 at 12 h, 41.2 at 24 h (Taiwo 2022).

variables.label: Mean arterial pressure
variables.notes: 47.2 at birth, 48.4 at 6 h, 50.2 at 12 h, 51.2 at 24 h (Taiwo 2022).

variables.label: Pulse pressure
variables.notes: SBP - DBP of the Taiwo means.

variables.label: Central venous pressure
variables.method: right atrial mean pressure, umbilical venous catheter
variables.notes: Healthy spontaneously breathing preterm infants (no term data; RAP did not correlate with birth weight or gestation). A-wave 4.9 (2-8). The 72 h textbook range 2-8 comes from sick infants.

variables.label: Pulmonary artery pressure, systolic
variables.notes: From the TR/ductal gradient. 24 h 43.8, 72 h 36.

variables.label: Pulmonary artery pressure, mean
variables.notes: PAP:SAP mean ~0.82 with the Taiwo MAP; ductal flow L->R only in 88 %.

variables.label: Pulmonary artery pressure, diastolic
variables.notes: Reference only.

variables.label: LV end-diastolic volume
variables.notes: No volumetric data at 12 h; the 72 h CMR values do not apply with a ~1.5x higher output.

variables.label: LV end-systolic volume
variables.notes: No volumetric data at 12 h; the 72 h CMR values do not apply with a ~1.5x higher output.

variables.label: LV ejection fraction
variables.notes: No volumetric data at 12 h; the 72 h CMR values do not apply with a ~1.5x higher output.

variables.label: RV end-diastolic volume
variables.notes: No volumetric data at 12 h; the 72 h CMR values do not apply with a ~1.5x higher output.

variables.label: RV end-systolic volume
variables.notes: No volumetric data at 12 h; the 72 h CMR values do not apply with a ~1.5x higher output.

variables.label: RV stroke volume
variables.notes: No volumetric data at 12 h; the 72 h CMR values do not apply with a ~1.5x higher output.

variables.label: RV ejection fraction
variables.notes: No volumetric data at 12 h; the 72 h CMR values do not apply with a ~1.5x higher output.

variables.label: Right ventricular output
variables.notes: No reliable term RVO at 12 h; with a left-to-right duct RVO < LVO.

variables.label: SVC flow
variables.notes: 99 at day 1, 77 at day 3.

variables.label: Descending aorta flow
variables.notes: No data at 12 h.

variables.label: Cerebral blood flow
variables.notes: MCA flow volume at 1 and 4-8 h lower than after 24 h; 12 h in between (Agata 1994; no number).

variables.label: Intestinal (SMA) flow
variables.notes: No data at 12 h.

variables.label: Renal blood flow
variables.method: Doppler volume flow, LEFT renal artery only
variables.notes: Agata 1994 Fig 2: left renal artery ~32 (24 h) and ~37 (96 h) mL/kg/min. Single-vessel Doppler volume flows are implausibly high in absolute terms (see sma), so no numeric reference; the stable time course is the usable finding.

variables.label: Hepatic arterial / coeliac flow
variables.notes: Agata 1994 Fig 2: coeliac ~75 (24 h), ~72 (96 h) mL/kg/min. Same absolute-overestimation caveat; coeliac also feeds the stomach and spleen.

variables.label: Respiratory rate
variables.notes: No healthy-term RR at 12 h found. 72 h reference kept (Schmalisch day 7: 39.2 +/- 8.6. Fleming: median 44 at birth.)

variables.label: Tidal volume
variables.notes: No 12 h data; Vt rises from day 0 to day 1 (Lodrup Carlsen 1993). 72 h reference kept (A face mask + pneumotach adds +13% Vt and +30% MV (Schmalisch 2001).)

variables.label: Minute ventilation
variables.notes: No 12 h data; Vt rises from day 0 to day 1 (Lodrup Carlsen 1993). 72 h reference kept ()

variables.label: Inspiratory time fraction (Ti/Ttot)
variables.notes: No 12 h data; Vt rises from day 0 to day 1 (Lodrup Carlsen 1993). 72 h reference kept ()

variables.label: Peak tidal inspiratory flow
variables.notes: No 12 h data; Vt rises from day 0 to day 1 (Lodrup Carlsen 1993). 72 h reference kept (The model ramps muscle pressure linearly over inspiration; infants peak earlier.)

variables.label: Peak tidal expiratory flow
variables.notes: No 12 h data; Vt rises from day 0 to day 1 (Lodrup Carlsen 1993). 72 h reference kept ()

variables.label: Respiratory system compliance
variables.notes: Crs lower on day 0 than from day 1 (direction only, no number); reference only.

variables.label: Respiratory system resistance
variables.notes: Rrs also lower on day 0 (Lodrup Carlsen 1993). 72 h reference kept (Katier (4.6 wk) ~75-80 (range 39-199).)

variables.label: Functional residual capacity
variables.method: argon dilution FRC; TGV by plethysmography
variables.notes: Lee 1999: 23.1 at 4-6 h, 24.9 at 24 h (vaginal).

variables.label: Anatomic dead space
variables.method: nasal mask, added dead space method
variables.notes: No 12 h data; Vt rises from day 0 to day 1 (Lodrup Carlsen 1993). 72 h reference kept (Vd/Vt ~0.3-0.4.)

variables.label: SpO2 (pre-ductal)
variables.notes: Median 98.3 over 0-24 h (O'Brien 2000); 96 +/- 1 at 1.5-13.5 h (Nikkola).

variables.label: pH
variables.notes: Textbook: the metabolic acidosis of birth is largely corrected by 12-24 h; no quotable measured values found.

variables.label: pCO2
variables.notes: Textbook: mild hypocapnia on day 1.

variables.label: Base excess
variables.notes: Textbook; no quotable measured values found.

variables.label: PaO2
variables.notes: No 12 h arterial data. 72 h reference kept (Capillary pO2 (Cousineau 45 +/- 7.5) is not comparable with arterial.)

variables.label: End-tidal CO2
variables.method: capnography; gap to PCO2 0 +/- 7 in healthy lungs
variables.notes: Expect EtCO2 ~ PaCO2.

variables.label: Mixed venous O2 saturation
variables.notes: Systemic extraction about as at 72 h (peripheral extraction constant over the first 24 h, Wolfsberger 2023): mixed systemic venous ~76-80 %; the pulmonary artery reads ~2 points higher with the left-to-right ductal admixture. Revised 2026-10-27 (was 85, 82-88, C).

variables.label: Oxygen consumption
variables.notes: The 72 h value (8.4, set from the venous extraction) plus first-day brown-fat thermogenesis in a 24 degC room (~0.9). Calorimetry 6.6-7.2 at 6-30 h, RQ 0.94 -> 0.88 (Zoppi 1998). Revised 2026-10-27 (was 7.0).

variables.label: Core temperature
variables.notes: Rectal lower on day 1 than day 2 (Fransson 2005).

variables.label: Plasma glucose
variables.notes: Mean rises over the first 18 h to a 3.3 +/- 0.6 plateau to 48 h; 2.6 ~ P10 (GLOW 2020).

variables.label: Lactate
variables.notes: GLOW 2021: 2.2 (1.1-6.2) over 0-12 h, 1.4 by 72 h; 12 h sits at the end of the first window.

variables.label: Hemoglobin
variables.notes: Scaled with the Hct (same red cell mass, see hct).

variables.label: Hematocrit
variables.notes: USER DECISION 2026-11-05 (option A): the 12 h baby is the same baby as term_neonate_72h, 60 h younger. Red cell mass held (72 h: Hct 49.5 x ~85 mL/kg = ~42 mL/kg); the plasma that leaves after birth partly returns over the next days, so Hct falls by the ratio 1.038 from 12 to 72 h (Nelle 1993, 3-min clamping: 58 at 2 h, 56 at 24 h, 54 at day 5 -> ~57.1 at 12 h vs ~55.0 at 72 h; Linderkamp 1992: 63 at 2 h, 59 at 24 h). 72 h value and range scaled by that ratio. Replaces the earlier 1-min DCC derivation (Hct 57, 77 mL/kg), which compared two clamping strategies, not one baby at two ages.

variables.label: Blood volume
variables.model_readout: sum of blood compartment volumes / weight
variables.notes: Red cell mass ~42 mL/kg held from 72 h; volume = 72 h volume / 1.038 (plasma not yet re-expanded). See hct.

variables.label: GFR
variables.notes: Day 1 value (30 at day 3, 40.6 at day 5); no hourly data.

variables.label: Urine output
variables.method: urine production before the postnatal diuresis
variables.notes: The postnatal diuresis starts at 7-22 h (Hogg 1977); 76 % have voided by 12 h (Ogala 1986).

variables.label: Ductal net left-to-right flow
variables.method: LV output minus systemic flow; orifice physics
variables.notes: USER DECISION 2026-11-05 (option A), replaces 5-40 (area scaling of Drayton, which ignored the rising gradient). Two estimates: (1) Agata LVO ~290 at 12 h (301 at 4-8 h, 245-272 at 24 h) against a systemic flow of ~200 (the 72 h LVO with the duct closed) leaves ~90 through the duct; (2) a 2.47 mm pulmonary end (Kang) with a ~2 m/s jet (Ha 2018) carries ~100-150 by orifice continuity, less with the viscous loss. Drayton 1987 (10 term): 62 (43-82) shortly after birth, falling rapidly over the first 12 h (direction only). Colour Doppler tends to overestimate small ductal diameters, which would put the true shunt at the low end. All L->R.

variables.label: Foramen ovale
variables.notes: Shunt in 92 % within 1 h, predominantly L->R with a small diastolic R->L component in 64 %; reference only.

variables.label: Ductal diameter
variables.notes: Kang 2016: 4.60 at 2 h, 3.37 at 6 h, 2.47 +/- 0.49 at 12 h, 1.89 at 24 h; open in 100 % at 12 h. Tohoku 2002: 2.1 +/- 0.6 at 12 h. Ha 2018 medians: 2.24 (1.72-2.71) over 0-12 h, 1.34 (1.2-1.73) over 12-24 h. Narrowing starts as a focal protrusion at the pulmonary end (96 % by 8 h) with a jet in and beyond it, then spreads along the duct (Hiraishi 1987; Rudolph). Target accepted by the user 2026-11-05 (Kang).

variables.label: Ductal right-to-left time
variables.notes: L->R only in 88 % at 12 h (Kang 2016); 3/19 still bidirectional at 12-24 h (Shiraishi 1991); some R->L up to 12 h (Walther 1993). Any R->L is systolic (Rudolph). van Laere: R->L < 30 % of the cycle = growing/bidirectional. Typical baby: none; a short systolic R->L is acceptable.

variables.label: Ductal peak L->R velocity
variables.method: PW/CW Doppler at the pulmonary end
variables.notes: Ha 2018 medians (IQR): 1.43 (1.07-1.78) over 0-12 h, 2.02 (1.49-2.26) over 12-24 h; 12 h sits between. Mandorla 1990: 1.5 +/- 0.7 at the first exam, 2.3 +/- 0.6 just before closure. Kang 2016 PA systolic 52.5 against Taiwo SBP 69.8 implies ~17 mmHg, ~2.1 m/s (derived). Velocity rises as the duct closes. Target accepted by the user 2026-11-05.

variables.label: Ductal end-diastolic L->R velocity
variables.method: Bernoulli from the aorta-PA diastolic gradient
variables.model_readout: beat minimum of Pda.velocity_doppler (a dip would show here)
variables.notes: No measured end-diastolic velocity at 12 h. Kang PA diastolic 23.4 against Taiwo DBP 40.4: ~17 mmHg, ~2.1 m/s (upper end). Mandorla: flow continuous or diastolic, flat or with a protosystolic/protodiastolic peak. Target accepted by the user 2026-11-05.

variables.label: Ductal peak / end-diastolic velocity
variables.notes: van Laere 2018 (after Su): closing < 2, pulsatile >= 2. A constricting duct at 12 h is expected near the border, closing to mildly pulsatile; Kang-derived gradients give ~1.0. Target accepted by the user 2026-11-05.

variables.label: SpO2 post-ductal
variables.notes: No pre/post-ductal gradient after 15 min (Mariani 2007).

variables.label: Coronary flow (whole heart)
variables.method: LAD volume flow by transthoracic Doppler (healthy controls, 1 week), scaled to the whole heart
variables.notes: LAD 8.2 +/- 3.0 mL/min (Aburawi 2012); the LAD carries ~35-45 % of the total, so ~18-23 mL/min; LAD flow per gram of LV is highest in young infants (Yasuoka 2002). Added 2026-10-27. 12 h: carried from 72 h (no first-day data); with a ~1.4x higher LV output and BP 70/40 expect the same or higher.

variables.label: Myocardial O2 use
variables.method: between adult resting values and newborn lambs
variables.notes: Newborn lambs (1 h): LV 18.9 mL/100 g/min, mechanical efficiency 31-35 % (Smolich 1996); adult rest ~8-10. Added 2026-10-27. 12 h: carried from 72 h.

variables.label: Pleural (oesophageal) pressure swing
variables.method: oesophageal water-filled catheter, quiet breathing; no change with growth from the newborn period to 5 years (n=40)
variables.model_readout: none in this probe: validate_respiratory base.ppl_swing (THORAX pressure swing per breath)
variables.notes: Cross-check: chest wall ~2.9x as compliant as the lung in infancy (Papastamelos 1995), so the model's Crs 0.96 mL/cmH2O/kg implies a lung compliance ~1.30 /kg against 1.34 +/- 0.37 measured in healthy term infants (Yau 1994); the elastic part of the swing is then Vt/CL ~4.4 cmH2O, the airway resistance adds the rest. Model 2026-10-28: 7.6 (+0.2 SD). Added 2026-10-28. 12 h: the earlier transitional work accepted 2-9 cmH2O (residual lung liquid, higher ventilation).

variables.label: Ventilatory response to CO2
variables.method: CO2 rebreathing (normoxic) in term babies at 4-6 days; quiet sleep 38.7 +/- 3.0, REM sleep 12.2 +/- 3.0 (n=5, 4-5 tests each)
variables.model_readout: none in this probe: scripts/probe_co2_response.mjs (steady state, 0/2/4 % inspired CO2)
variables.notes: Mixed sleep/awake state between the REM and quiet-sleep values; test-to-test variation 35 % in quiet sleep. Moriette 1985 (rebreathing in 40 % O2) 67 in quiet sleep, 44 in active sleep: upper bound. Steady-state and rebreathing slopes agree in preterms (38 vs 40, Rigatto 1991). Pattern: Vt rises in all reports; rate contributes in quiet sleep (Cohen 1991: the REM deficit is mainly a missing rate rise), little in preterms and newborn mammals (Rigatto 1981; Mortola 1996: Vt +78 %, rate 98 % at 5 % CO2); no quantitative term split found. Model 2026-10-28: 34 (0-4 % CO2; RR +52 %, Vt +35 % at 4 %). Added 2026-10-28. 12 h: carried from 72 h (cross-check only).

variables.label: Respiratory quotient
variables.method: indirect calorimetry (VCO2 / VO2 at the airway)
variables.notes: Zoppi 1998: 0.94 at 6 h, 0.88 at 30 h (term, before milk); 12 h interpolated ~0.92. Breastfeeding just started. The model resp_q 0.80 sits below.
